subject: Chemistry
topic: Question reel: which reacts faster by SN1 or SN2?
title: Which Reacts Faster by SN1 or SN2? 5 Solved Questions
summary: A question set: two rules, five pairs, each solved with a reason. In this lesson: the two rules (SN2: least crowding; SN1: most stable carbocation) and the leaving group order I ＞ Br ＞ Cl, then five solved pairs: 1- vs 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-3-methylbutane vs 1-bromo-2-methylbutane, 2-bromopropane vs 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, benzyl chloride vs 1-chloro-1-phenylethane, ethyl chloride vs ethyl iodide.

notes.title: Which Reacts Faster by SN1 or SN2? 5 Solved Questions
notes.blurb: the two rules, solved pairs, more orders worth knowing

keyPoints: **SN2 rule**: 1-bromobutane **beats** 2-bromobutane. A branch **next to C–X** also slows it.
**Leaving group**: Same alkyl group: **ethyl iodide** fastest. True for **SN1 and SN2**.
**Trap**: Both are **1°**: look at the branch. The nearer branch **blocks the back**.

list: **SN2** (backside attack): less crowding at and next to the carbon = faster. CH₃X > 1° > 2° > 3°; a branch on the carbon next to C–X also slows it.
**SN1** (carbocation first): the more stable the carbocation, the faster. 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃X; allylic and benzylic carbocations are resonance-stabilised.
**Leaving group** (both): R–I > R–Br > R–Cl > R–F, because the C–X bond weakens from F to I.

blocks.p: SN1 among benzylic bromides: C₆H₅C(CH₃)(C₆H₅)Br > C₆H₅CH(C₆H₅)Br > C₆H₅CH(CH₃)Br > C₆H₅CH₂Br. SN2 among the bromobutanes: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂Br > (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Br > CH₃CH₂CH(Br)CH₃ > (CH₃)₃CBr.

list: ✗ Two 1° halides always react at the same SN2 rate (a branch next to C–X slows the reaction).
✗ R–Cl is the best leaving group because Cl is most electronegative (R–I is the most reactive: the weakest C–X bond).

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.

pyq.q: Assertion (A): SN2 reaction of C₆H₅CH₂Br occurs more readily than the SN2 reaction of CH₃CH₂Br. Reason (R): The partially bonded unhybridized p-orbital that develops in the trigonal bipyramidal transition state is stabilized by conjugation with the phenyl ring.
options: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
pyq.explain: In the SN2 transition state the carbon carries a p orbital partly bonded to Nu and Br; in benzyl bromide it overlaps with the ring π system, lowering the energy. Both true, R explains A.

pyq.q: Assertion A: Hydrolysis of an alkyl chloride is a slow reaction but in the presence of NaI, the rate of hydrolysis increases. Reason R: I⁻ is a good nucleophile as well as a good leaving group.
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
pyq.explain: I⁻ first displaces Cl⁻ quickly (good nucleophile), then the C–I bond is hydrolysed quickly (good leaving group); NaI is regenerated.
